policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: Article with the place name Amphipolis; ASV 'when they had passed through Amphipolis' renders the proper noun alone either way. Nothing in the English marks the article.
ASV 'where was a synagogue of the Jews' is indefinite; the added article of r01 (ἦν ἡ συναγωγή) would give 'the synagogue'.

The readings differ only in punctuation and in the article on χριστός. ASV 'is the Christ' renders the title definitely whether or not ὁ stands, and 'this Jesus, whom ... I proclaim' fits both the appositional and the attributive arrangements.
Word order only; ASV 'a great multitude' is the same English for πλῆθος πολύ and πολὺ πλῆθος.
ASV has 'the Jews, being moved with jealousy, took unto them' — ζηλώσαντες is rendered and there is no equivalent of RP's οἱ ἀπειθοῦντες ('which believed not').
Word order only; ASV 'certain vile fellows' is the same for ἄνδρας τινάς and τινὰς ἄνδρας.
Connective only; ASV 'and assaulting the house of Jason' renders καί or the postpositive τε alike.
ASV 'to bring them forth to the people' carries the directional 'forth' answering the προ- of προαγαγεῖν; bare ἀγαγεῖν εἰς τὸν δῆμον would be simply 'to bring to the people'.
Article with the proper name Jason; ASV 'they dragged Jason' shows nothing either way.
Word order only; ASV 'saying that there is another king' is the same for ἕτερον λέγοντες and λέγοντες ἕτερον.
Article within the prepositional phrase; ASV 'by night' renders διὰ νυκτός and διὰ τῆς νυκτός identically.
Word order only; ASV 'went into the synagogue of the Jews' is the same for either sequence.
Article on the adverbial καθ' ἡμέραν; ASV 'daily' does not show it.
ASV 'stirring up and troubling the multitudes' renders καὶ ταράσσοντες, which r01 omits.
ASV 'to go as far as to the sea' renders ἕως ἐπὶ τὴν θάλασσαν; RP's ὡς would give 'as it were to the sea'.
Aorist with τε against imperfect with δέ; ASV 'and Silas and Timothy abode there still' distinguishes neither the tense nor the connective, both of which it renders 'and ... abode'.
Alternate present-participle formations of the same verb; ASV 'they that conducted Paul' fits both.

ASV 'brought him as far as Athens' has an unitalicized 'him', but the pronoun equally resumes the preceding τὸν Παῦλον as required English idiom, so it does not settle whether αὐτόν stood in the Greek.
Article with the proper name Silas; ASV 'unto Silas and Timothy' shows nothing either way.
Genitive-absolute against dative participle construction; ASV 'his spirit was provoked within him as he beheld' renders both alike.

Article before the second adjective; ASV 'the Epicurean and Stoic philosophers' does not mark whether the article was repeated. The verse's notes are an alternative rendering, a Greek gloss, and a cross-reference, none of which touches this unit.
Connective only; ASV 'And they took hold of him' renders τε and δέ alike, and the two notes are alternative renderings of Ἄρειον Πάγον.
ASV 'we would know therefore what these things mean' shows no potential optative and no interrogative number distinction; τίνα θέλει and τί ἂν θέλοι both yield it.
ASV 'either to tell or to hear' renders ἤ; RP's καί would give 'and to hear'.
ASV 'some new thing' renders the indefinite τι with καινότερον, which r01 omits.
Article with the proper name Paul; ASV 'And Paul stood' shows nothing either way, and the verse's note is an alternative rendering of δεισιδαιμονεστέρους.
ASV 'What therefore ye worship in ignorance' is neuter ὅ; RP's masculine ὅν would give 'whom therefore ye worship'.
ASV 'this I set forth unto you' is neuter τοῦτο, answering the neuter relative; RP's τοῦτον would give 'him I set forth'.
Word order only; ASV 'he, being Lord of heaven and earth' is the same for either sequence.
Adjective ἀνθρωπίναις against genitive ἀνθρώπων; ASV 'by men's hands' renders both.
ASV 'giveth to all life, and breath, and all things' renders καὶ τὰ πάντα as a third object; RP's κατὰ πάντα would be adverbial ('in all things') and yield no 'and all things'.
ASV 'he made of one every nation of men' has no 'blood'; RP's ἑνὸς αἵματος would give 'of one blood'.
Genitive against accusative after ἐπί with the same words; ASV 'on all the face of the earth' renders both.
ASV 'that they should seek God' renders θεόν; RP's κύριον would give 'the Lord'.
ASV text 'he commandeth men' renders παραγγέλλει, and the mapped textual note 'Some ancient authorities read declareth to men' puts ἀπαγγέλλει in the margin, not the text.

ASV 'commandeth men that they should all everywhere repent' attaches 'all' to the infinitive clause, i.e. accusative πάντας as its subject; RP's dative πᾶσιν would agree with τοῖς ἀνθρώποις and give 'commandeth all men everywhere to repent'.
Causal conjunctions of the same force; ASV 'inasmuch as' renders καθότι and διότι alike, and the verse's notes are Greek glosses and an alternative rendering.
Word order only; ASV 'concerning this yet again' is the same for either sequence.
ASV 'Thus Paul went out from among them' begins with no conjunction, rendering οὕτως alone rather than RP's καὶ οὕτως.
